description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Storage Platform Engineer based in United States. 

 In this role, you will own the architecture and build of a software-defined, NVMe-over-Fabrics storage platform that sits beneath millions of Postgres databases. The goal is near-local-NVMe performance with the durability and flexibility of networked storage, all without modifying Postgres itself. You will drive the work end to end, from build-vs-buy decisions and integration into a Kubernetes-based compute platform to running the system in production. Over time, the layer you build will power block-level snapshots, copy-on-write clones, database branching, fast restores, and instant resizes across multiple clouds and colocated infrastructure. This is a foundational, high-ownership position where you will set the technical direction for storage and help grow the team around it. The role is fully remote within a born-remote, open-source-first, globally distributed company of roughly 400 people across more than 60 countries.



Accountabilities
 

 Lead the architecture of the NVMe-oF storage platform, including evaluating and deciding between adopting existing software-defined storage and building on SPDK.

 Integrate networked block storage into a Kubernetes-based compute platform through CSI drivers and custom controllers, covering provisioning, attach/detach, resizing, and migration.

 Make Postgres fast on networked storage by profiling and tuning the full I/O path, from fsync, WAL, and checkpoints through the kernel block layer, NVMe/TCP, and the network.

 Design for durability and availability, including replication or erasure coding, failure domains, failover, and data-integrity verification.

 Build I/O isolation and QoS so that noisy neighbors cannot degrade other tenants.

 Set performance and reliability SLOs, and build the benchmarking and observability needed to hold the system to them.

 Design the layer for block-level snapshots and copy-on-write clones, laying the groundwork for database branching.

 Keep the platform portable across AWS, other clouds, and bare-metal/colo environments.

 Write design docs, mentor engineers, and work closely with the Compute, Branching, Postgres, and Multicloud teams.

 Participate in on-call rotations, incident response, and post-incident reviews.

 Resolve escalated support issues while identifying and fixing systemic issues across the platform.


 Requirements


 7+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and operating storage systems in production.

 Experience building or operating distributed or software-defined block storage (for example Ceph RBD, Lightbits, Simplyblock, Portworx, LINSTOR/DRBD, or an in-house system).

 Hands-on experience with NVMe/TCP or NVMe-oF, including targets, initiators, multipath, and failover behavior.

 Deep understanding of Linux storage internals: the block layer, io_uring, page cache, O_DIRECT and fsync semantics, filesystems, and device-mapper.

 Strong systems programming skills in Go, plus C, C++, or Rust.

 Rigorous performance measurement using fio, pgbench, eBPF, and perf, with the ability to explain latency down to its individual components.

 Solid understanding of durability tradeoffs between replication, erasure coding, and consistency under failure.

 Experience leading technical direction on a complex system, including design docs, tradeoffs, and bringing others along.

 Experience with Kubernetes controllers and/or CSI drivers.

 Experience being on call for large production systems.

 Clear written communication and the ability to thrive in asynchronous, globally distributed teams.

 Located in India.

 Nice to have: SPDK development experience.

 Nice to have: RDMA/RoCE experience.

 Nice to have: Experience implementing block-level snapshots, thin provisioning, or copy-on-write cloning.

 Nice to have: Postgres internals knowledge (WAL, buffer manager, checkpointer), or familiarity with OrioleDB.

 Nice to have: Experience with AWS networking and instance storage at scale (ENA, placement, bandwidth limits).

 Nice to have: Experience running storage on bare metal or in colo.

 Nice to have: Contributions to open source storage projects or the Linux kernel storage stack.


 Benefits


 Fully remote work with no offices, plus a WeWork membership or co-working allowance usable anywhere in the world.

 Equity ownership (ESOP) for every team member.

 Tech allowance for laptop, monitor, headphones, or other home-office needs.

 Health insurance covered 100% for employees and 80% for dependents.

 Annual company off-site in a new city each year.

 Flexible, asynchronous work with trust to manage your own time.

 Annual education allowance for courses, books, conferences, or other learning.

 Open-source-first culture with a globally distributed team across 60+ countries.
